stories.author: shscs911
stories.title: Android May Soon Restrict On-Device ADB
stories.groq_label: Google may restrict on-device ADB connections to protect against potential security threats.
stories.groq_discussion:
Discussion type: – Basic:

This proposal to restrict on-device ADB on Android is aimed at solving the problem of user security. Based on the Hacker News discussion, commenters generally viewed the initiative negatively, expressing concerns about the practical implications of limiting user choices. Many appreciated the idea of restricting access to certain interfaces or IP addresses, but criticized the decision to restrict ADB entirely, arguing that this would unnecessarily hinder user flexibility and innovation. Some commenters believed that this decision would set a concerning precedent for future restrictions on device functionality, while others feared that it would lead to a decrease in Android's customizability and user experience. The discussion also highlighted concerns that this restriction could be used as a means to lock users into specific apps or services. Overall, the Hacker News community considered the proposal to be overly restrictive and counterproductive, emphasizing the need for a more nuanced approach that balances security with user choice and flexibility.
stories.groq_explain: Google might restrict how Android users connect to the Android Debug Bridge (ADB) on their own devices, supposedly to prevent bad actors from exploiting it.

The overall discussion suggests that the community sees value in the leaderboard but believes that its results should be viewed with caution and considered in the context of real-world applications.

stories.author: KraftyOne
stories.title: Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY actually scales
stories.groq_label: Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY achieves 60K writes per second with millisecond-scale latency after optimizing it with a custom patch to change its semantics.
stories.groq_discussion:
Discussion type: – Balanced:

This article/project aims to solve the problem of assessing the scalability of the Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY feature. The Hacker News discussion was generally mixed, with many commenters appreciating the project's customization of Postgres to meet its requirements and the potential benefits of durable workflows. However, the discussion also raised concerns about the limitations of LISTEN/NOTIFY, including its hard limit on notification data size and potential issues with batching commands. Commenters debated the meaning of "scaling" in the context of LISTEN/NOTIFY, suggesting it is not a binary concept and may vary significantly based on specific needs and use cases. The discussion highlighted the need for further refinement and customization of the feature to better meet real-world requirements.
stories.groq_explain: Postgres' LISTEN/NOTIFY has a bad reputation for not scaling, but the author of this article shows that it actually can handle a large number of writes and low latency, even on a single server, if optimized properly. This matters because LISTEN/NOTIFY is a powerful tool for notification and streams in databases.
